gaps.fact: Tuscany's coast faces the Ligurian Sea in the north and the Tyrrhenian in the south. The Tyrrhenian is in the article and one explanation; the Ligurian Sea is never tied to Tuscany and stands only as a distractor in i-vlg5as98.

Montalcino: clay and marine sediments at lower elevation, galestro at higher elevation. The article says only varied marine, sedimentary and stony ground; no chapter fact or stem ties galestro to Montalcino's upper slopes.

Sangiovese based wines show moderate colour, tart acidity that outweighs the tannin, and volatile acidity is common in them. The chapter gives the colour and the acid; volatile acidity in Sangiovese appears nowhere (the faults table names Amarone and Sauternes for it).

Rosso di Montepulciano DOC, the younger wine beneath Vino Nobile, and the several Vin Santo DOCs (Vin Santo del Chianti, del Chianti Classico, di Montepulciano among them). Only the article's law tier and one wine line name them; no chapter fact and no stem.
Ruffino, one of the Court's three Introductory names, appears nowhere in the Codex.

Soldera and Le Pergole Torte stand only in the article (the Court prints La Pergole Torte), Banfi in the article and as a distractor; no stem asks a Brunello house beyond Biondi-Santi, though the Court asks the candidate to recognise the important ones.
The top Brunello di Montalcino vintages of the past fifteen years. No chapter, stem, article line or card rates a Montalcino vintage; a dated card is the right home.

The current release of Brunello di Montalcino (the vintage on the market now, released each January of the fifth year after harvest) and the approximate price of the top proprietary brands. The release rule is taught; the current vintage and the price band are not, and both move every year.

errors.where: js/data-questions.js, QUESTIONS c-wpxpyzl1, stem: "Outside the Classico zone the Sangiovese minimum sits at seventy percent." and explanation: "The wider Chianti DOCG stays at seventy."
errors.claim: Chianti DOCG requires at least 70 per cent Sangiovese.
errors.correction: The amended Chianti DOCG rules, published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 13 June 2026, lower the minimum to 60 per cent from the 2026/27 harvest campaign (with a new Terre di Vinci sub-zone and a rosé); earlier vintages keep the 70 per cent rule, and the Court's guide still prints 70. The key (Chianti Classico at 80) is unaffected; the explanation should give both figures, and the tuscany article already does.
errors.source: Chianti DOCG disciplinare as amended, Gazzetta Ufficiale 13 June 2026; gamberorosso.it, 16 June 2026; meininger.de and thedrinksbusiness.com, 2026; the Codex's own tuscany article (law, tiers).

errors.where: js/data-primers.js, PRIMERS cat Italy Central & South, fact Chianti: "A separate and larger DOCG around the Classico zone, at least 70 per cent Sangiovese, with subzones such as Rufina and Colli Senesi."
errors.claim: Chianti DOCG requires at least 70 per cent Sangiovese.
errors.correction: At least 60 per cent from the 2026/27 harvest campaign under the June 2026 amendment, 70 per cent for earlier vintages and on the Court's printed page; the sub-zones now number eight with Terre di Vinci.
errors.source: Chianti DOCG disciplinare as amended, Gazzetta Ufficiale 13 June 2026; gamberorosso.it, 16 June 2026; the Codex's own tuscany article (law, tiers; places).

courtUpdates.now: Chianti DOCG requires at least 60 per cent Sangiovese from the 2026/27 harvest campaign, adds an eighth sub-zone, Terre di Vinci, and admits a rosé; the amended rules were published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale on 13 June 2026.
courtUpdates.source: Gazzetta Ufficiale, 13 June 2026; gamberorosso.it, novità Chianti DOCG, 16 June 2026; meininger.de, weniger Sangiovese im Chianti; thedrinksbusiness.com, May 2026.

courtUpdates.now: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano has a top tier, Pieve: at least 85 per cent Sangiovese (Prugnolo Gentile) with native red partners only, estate fruit from one named pieve zone, three years of ageing; approved by the national wine committee on 3 August 2023 and first on the market on 1 January 2025 with the 2021 vintage.
courtUpdates.source: Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, press kit 2025 (consorziovinonobile.it); rivistadiagraria.org, the ministry approves the Pieve disciplinare; meininger.de, Montepulciano hebt Pieve aus der Taufe.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (Italy), Village 61 (Italy Central & South), 122 in all; both categories are shared with the other Italian subjects, and by stem the Tuscan share is 10 Régionale (i-z1mguxwd, i-vf1cinrg, i-qsjgs92z, i-lefucj4u, i-ww86dcdf, i-766ij290, i-7b15euma, i-w4z81d93, i-kgnfu8ii, i-e40905u8) and 21 Village. Beyond the map: Producers & Icons asks Antinori, Sassicaia and Biondi-Santi; History & Figures Ricasoli, the Medici edict and the eighteenth century boundaries; Dessert & Sweet Wines, Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet and Sweet Wines carry six Vin Santo stems; Food & Pairing Chianti with tomato. Tuscany is the most thoroughly drilled Italian subject: the three Sangiovese DOCGs, Gran Selezione, the Super Tuscans and their grapes all have Village stems. The thin cells are the Montalcino soil split, volatile acidity, Rosso di Montepulciano and the Vin Santo DOCs, Ruffino and the Brunello houses, and the two volatile cells (vintages, current release and price). Court cells to read with care: the Court prints Rosso di Montalcino DOCG in the Introductory cell, while it is a DOC (as the article teaches); La Pergole Torte is the Court's spelling of Le Pergole Torte; and the Court's 70 per cent for Chianti is now the older rule (logged above). Two searches spent, both on law: the Chianti amendment of June 2026 and the Vino Nobile Pieve tier. The article also teaches the Gran Selezione move to 90 per cent Sangiovese with native partners from the 2027 vintage and the 2026 Morellino amendment; the Court asks only that Gran Selezione exists, so neither is logged as a court update.
